mainEntity.name: What is weld project structure software?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is the tool that models a fabrication project — assemblies, parts and the joints between them — so every weld and work entry has a place to live and a traceable path upward to the finished piece. Elenchon runs it on-premise, on hardware you own.

mainEntity.name: Can I import a BOM from Tekla or CAD?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Copy your BOM straight out of Tekla or your CAD package and paste it into an Excel-like grid. Elenchon auto-detects the columns, maps every field, and builds the project structure in seconds — no special export format needed.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the tree and flowchart views?

acceptedAnswer.text: They are two editable windows onto the same project. The tree is a left-indented outline suited to detailed one-off structures; the flowchart is a visual, drag-to-connect editor suited to standardized, repeatable ones. Edit either and the other updates instantly.

mainEntity.name: Can I edit a project after work has started?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can add nodes or remove empty ones on an in-progress project, while any node that already contains captured work is automatically locked and protected — so the structure evolves without rewriting history.

mainEntity.name: Does it handle repeatable batches and one-offs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both. Define an assembly once and deploy identical copies in quantity for batch production, or build a fully bespoke tree for a one-off — welds defined once on a repeated assembly apply to every copy.
